For a function to be continuous over an entire interval, it has to be continuous on every point in that interval.

Graphically, this is roughly the same as being able to draw the graph of the function on that interval without lifting the pencil.

![Function g is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve and 2 closed circles. The curve starts in quadrant 2, moves downward to about (negative 5, negative 7), moves upward through an open circle at about (negative 3, negative 4.8) and an open circle at (0, 3) to an open circle at (3, 7), moves downward, and ends at about (8, 0). Closed circles are plotted at (negative 3, 3) and (3, 3).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/b5fbd81847192d58a3bfc14904e343c0c2af2842)

The value $g(0)$ is undefined, so $g$ isn't continuous at $x=0$.

Since $g$ isn't continuous on one of the points in $[-2,0]$, it isn't continuous over that interval.

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 3}g(x)\neq g(3)$. Therefore, $g$ isn't continuous at $x=3$.

Since $g$ isn't continuous on one of the points in $[1,5]$, it isn't continuous over that interval.

In conclusion, $g$ is not continuous over either interval. 

The answer is none of the above.
